t: MOON: Multi-Objective Optimization-Driven Object-Goal Navigation Using a Variable-Horizon Set-Orienteering Planner
size: n/a (solver); distilled student: 6-layer, 8-head, d_model=128 transformer (parameter count not given)
obs: Main text: abstract 2D world with circular sensing, i.e. a long-range landmark detector (L=100/200 m) and a short-range target detector (R=3 m, results also given for R=10), plus known pose. Appendix A: 360° depth up to 8 m for mapping, 90°-FOV landmark detection at 8 m, and a 90° target cone at 1 m (forward RGB-like sensor + omnidirectional depth). Appendix B: range sensing + depth fused into a semantic occupancy grid.
act: High-level subgoal selection: the next viewpoint node on the landmark navigation graph or a frontier cell, executed by a Dijkstra/A* global planner and a local planner.
priv: Robot self-location assumed known. Landmark and target detection are idealized, noise-free fixed-radius sensors in the main 2D experiments. A given target–landmark co-occurrence prior P(Target|Landmark) is used in Appendix A.
extra: Own abstract 2D benchmark with 100 randomized trials; long-range landmark sensor L=100 m, target sensor R=3 m, M=10 landmarks, known pose, single point target. Only baseline with meaningful SPL: Frontier 0.6083. Printed as a fraction.
ev: Results bullet list: 'L=100, R=3, M=10 ... Frontieer: 0.6083 ... MOON: 0.8315'
cmp_why: Own benchmark; nothing beyond its protocol

t: ProcWorld: Benchmarking Large Model Planning in Reachability-Constrained Environments
obs: Text mode: symbolic NL descriptions of visible objects with 2D coordinates, reachable frontier locations, doors, object states and containment relations (360° view). Vision mode: annotated 360° panoramas with frontier markers plus object-centric RGB views. Vision-LLM variant: text converted from oracle depth and instance segmentation.
act: Discrete high-level language actions: go to frontier location / go to surrounding object / go through door / interact with facing object (pick, place, open, close, toggle, slice, heat, cool, clean). Interaction and visibility are limited by a radius (inf, 3m, 1.5m). 50-step budget.
priv: Frontier waypoints, object coordinates, object states and containment relations are given symbolically (text mode). The vision-LLM variant uses oracle depth and instance segmentation. The infinite-reach setting allows teleportation, and the map-based settings provide a dynamic topological map of visited locations.
extra: Text environment; SR at infinite reach (full), 3m (map-free) and 1.5m (map-free). The paper labels these 'state-of-the-art LLMs'; the values equal the mean of Qwen2.5-72B over ReAct/AgentBench/StateFlow/ALFChat/Reflexion in Tables 3,5,7,9,11. 50-step budget.
ev: Sec. 4.2: "for the state-of-the-art LLMs, the average success rate drops 53.19%, from 81.19% (full) to 38.03% (partial, 3m), and further drops 49.72%, from 38.03% (partial, 3m) to 19.12% (partial, 1.5m)"

t: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
obs: VLA: monocular single-view RGB (current frame + uniformly sampled history, 8-64 frames; 8 in real world); no depth, panorama or odometry. Locomotion: proprioception history + 2.5D height map from 360° LiDAR (Go2) / height scan (H1 in sim).
act: Mid-level language actions (move forward X cm, turn left/right X degrees, stop), parsed by regex. On the robot these become velocity commands (0.5 m/s, ±π/6 rad/s) held for the matching duration, then 12-DoF desired joint positions from the RL policy. In Habitat VLN-CE they are executed as continuous forward/turn moves.
priv: none at test time (privileged terrain heights used only by the RL critic during training)
extra: single-view RGB only; trained with R2R-CE + RxR-CE + EnvDrop aug + ScanQA + VQA + 20K YouTube human-video trajectories
ev: Table 1 'Comparison with state-of-the-art methods on the Val-Unseen split of R2R-CE and RxR-CE'; also Table 'Results on R2R-CE using additional real data from human touring videos'

t: GRUtopia: Dream General Robots in a City at Scale
size: mixed (e.g., Llama-3 8B in the agent; GPT-4o size undisclosed; NPCs use InternLM2-Chat-20B / Llama-3-70B / GPT-4o)
obs: egocentric RGB-D (H1 head camera; for Aliengo, a camera on a pole 0.8 m above the base) + robot state; the VLM baseline uses only the current RGB frame + text prompt
act: VLM baseline: 12 discrete macro-actions (move forward / advance diagonally left/right 2/4/6 m, turn left/right 90°, stop) + Ask (social) + Pick/Place (manipulation). LLM agent: choose a candidate goal object, then an RRT* path executed as continuous legged locomotion by the RL controller; IK arm control for pick/place.
priv: The agent receives the robot state/pose. The Social task uses an oracle LLM NPC with full scene-graph knowledge. A fallen robot is reset to standing (counted as RT). Grasping is simplified: the object attaches to the gripper within a distance threshold. No GT map or semantics is given to the agent (SegFormer perception, online occupancy map).
extra: Unitree H1 with RL locomotion controller; SegFormer grounding + BEV occupancy map + RRT*; robot state input; TL = paper's PL
ev: Table 4 'Quantitative results in GRBench using VLM baselines and LLM agent baselines', validation, LLM GPT-4o row
cmp_why: No GT map or semantics; pose is standard

obs: egocentric RGB-D (H1 head camera; for Aliengo, a camera on a pole 0.8 m above the base) + robot state; the VLM baseline uses only the current RGB frame + text prompt
act: VLM baseline: 12 discrete macro-actions (move forward / advance diagonally left/right 2/4/6 m, turn left/right 90°, stop) + Ask (social) + Pick/Place (manipulation). LLM agent: choose a candidate goal object, then an RRT* path executed as continuous legged locomotion by the RL controller; IK arm control for pick/place.
priv: The agent receives the robot state/pose. The Social task uses an oracle LLM NPC with full scene-graph knowledge. A fallen robot is reset to standing (counted as RT). Grasping is simplified: the object attaches to the gripper within a distance threshold. No GT map or semantics is given to the agent (SegFormer perception, online occupancy map).
extra: Up to 3 dialogue rounds with an oracle LLM NPC

t: An Embodied Generalist Agent in 3D World
size: ~7B total (~142M trainable); ablations with OPT-1.3B and Vicuna-13B

ev: Table 'Results on object navigation' (MP3D-val Success / SPL); also 'LEO (shortest)' in appendix table 'Results on object navigation with OOD objects and human demonstrations'
cmp_why: Global object point clouds = pre-scanned map

t: R2H: Building Multimodal Navigation Helpers that Respond to Help Requests
backbone: SwinBERT-initialized Video Swin + BERT multimodal transformer (fine-tuned)
obs: Helper: an oracle image sequence of performer views along the shortest path to the goal (CVDN ≤5 viewpoints ahead; AVDN north-up top-down drone views with heading arrow) plus the text inquiry and dialog. Performers use their native observations (e.g., HAMT panoramic RGB).
act: Helper outputs free-form natural-language responses. Performers act in native spaces: CVDN nav-graph viewpoints, DialFRED/AI2-THOR discrete actions, AVDN continuous drone waypoints.
priv: Helper uses oracle information by design: goal location and shortest-path image sequences sampled from the environment/connectivity graph. Performers get no privileged info.
extra: Helper-agent task: responses replace human answers in CVDN NDH dialog history; fixed HAMT performer pre-trained on CVDN NDH; helper sees oracle shortest-path image sequence; trained on GPT-3 Parse-by-Step responses. Human-annotator reference: GP 6.9, SPL 17.6, SR 20.7.
ev: Table 1 (RDH results) and appendix table 'Results of Respond to Dialog History (RDH) task on CVDN dataset (a)'; B2/ROUGE-L from ablation table (COS ✓, Parse by Step ✓ row)
cmp_why: Oracle helper is by design of R2H benchmark

t: Can an Embodied Agent Find Your "Cat-shaped Mug"? LLM-Guided Exploration for Zero-Shot Object Navigation

t: Consistent Attack: Universal Adversarial Perturbation on Embodied Vision Navigation
method: Reward UAP (attack on RGB PPO victim)
backbone: habitat-baselines PPO PointNav agent (RGB), frozen victim
obs: egocentric RGB or depth (separate victims) + PointGoal target (GPS/compass-style goal vector as in habitat-baselines)

cmp_why: Attack robustness evaluation; victim uses standard inputs

t: Semantic Exploration from Language Abstractions and Pretrained Representations
backbone: R2D2 ResNet+LSTM policy; frozen Small-ALM image encoder for intrinsic reward
size: policy small (ResNet channels 16/32/32, LSTM 256); reward encoders frozen: Small-ALM 25M ResNet image + 44M BERT text, Med-ALM 71M NFNet + 77M BERT, CLIP; ImageNet control 71M NFNet-F0

extra: No official split; a new map is procedurally generated each episode. Pure exploration with no extrinsic reward, 11,250-step episodes. Coverage = unique bins of a 32x32 grid (1024 bins, not all reachable), mean ± s.e. over 5 replicas.

t: TEACh: Task-driven Embodied Agents that Chat
obs: egocentric RGB (900x900, resized to 224 for ResNet / 300 for Mask R-CNN) + concatenated dialogue history + past actions

t: Navigation Turing Test (NTT): Learning to Evaluate Human-Like Navigation

t: VOILA: Visual-Observation-Only Imitation Learning for Autonomous Navigation
backbone: ResNet-18 RAE + MLP SAC policy (RGB camera input)
obs: Monocular front-facing RGB (256×256) encoded to a 512-d latent, 2 frames stacked, plus previous action; LIDAR range scans in the VOILA-lidar variant
act: Continuous change in steering and throttle
priv: none at test time. During training only: the expert demo is used for the reward, crash detection comes from AirSim or a human trainer, and the robot is manually reset between episodes.
extra: Expert is a video from a human walking with a handheld phone camera (egocentric viewpoint mismatch). Rollout is in the training environment. Metric is the Hausdorff distance between expert and rollout trajectories (lower is better); reference values: Suboptimal 0.806, Random 1.192.
ev: TABLE I: Hausdorff distance between the expert trajectory and the policy rollout trajectory of VOILA (row 'human demo | VOILA | 0.783')

t: Pathdreamer: A World Model for Indoor Navigation
backbone: RCM-based agent beam search + instruction-trajectory compatibility model + Pathdreamer imagined RGB
obs: 360° equirectangular panoramas: RGB + depth + semantic segmentation as context, with known camera poses. The VLN agent sees panoramic RGB.
act: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (R2R); the world model is conditioned on arbitrary future 6-DoF poses
priv: GT depth and semantic segmentation (rendered from the annotated MP3D mesh) for observed context panoramas, plus GT camera poses. In VLN, the geometry of future trajectories, including unvisited regions, comes from the ground-truth R2R navigation graph. Checkpoints are selected on the respective validation split.
extra: Look-ahead planning: beam-search candidate trajectories along the GT nav graph (future geometry from the GT graph) are ranked with Pathdreamer-predicted RGB for 3 future steps; execute first action then replan. Not a standard single-pass agent.
ev: Table 3 'VLN Val-Unseen results using an instruction-trajectory compatibility model ... planning horizons of 1, 2 or 3 steps', row Pathdreamer, Plan Steps 3
cmp_why: Beam search with lookahead over GT graph

t: HRL4IN: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Interactive Navigation with Mobile Manipulators
bench: Interactive Gibson Environment (Interactive Navigation, door opening)
backbone: CNN+GRU PPO hierarchical policies (trained from scratch)
obs: Gibson: 64×64 depth map (clipped at 5 m) + proprioception (end-effector xyz, base pose/velocities, roll/pitch/yaw, joint positions/velocities/torques, collision and grasp flags) + door angle/location + goal location. ToyEnv: 4-channel top-down global map + agent pose + door state + goal.
act: Gibson: continuous joint velocities for 2 wheels + 5 arm joints (7 DoF), with an automatic grasp primitive. ToyEnv: discrete turn-left/turn-right/go-forward/no-op + slide-up/slide-down/no-op.
priv: Door angle and location, goal position and robot/end-effector poses come directly from the simulator state; ToyEnv provides a full top-down global map. A scripted grasp primitive attaches to the door handle when the end-effector is within 0.1 m. Training and evaluation use the same single layout.
extra: Single fixed training/evaluation layout; success radius 0.5 m; max episode length 1000; grasp primitive; privileged door/goal state in observation. Energy-Saving is a fraction (symbolic energy units), Reward is episode return.
ev: Table 1 'Ablation Study Results for Interactive Gibson Environment': HRL4IN (full), All reward terms, Success Rate 0.963, Reward 64.3, Energy-Saving 0.453
cmp_why: Privileged state is part of this custom environment

obs: Gibson: 64×64 depth map (clipped at 5 m) + proprioception (end-effector xyz, base pose/velocities, roll/pitch/yaw, joint positions/velocities/torques, collision and grasp flags) + door angle/location + goal location. ToyEnv: 4-channel top-down global map + agent pose + door state + goal.
act: Gibson: continuous joint velocities for 2 wheels + 5 arm joints (7 DoF), with an automatic grasp primitive. ToyEnv: discrete turn-left/turn-right/go-forward/no-op + slide-up/slide-down/no-op.
priv: Door angle and location, goal position and robot/end-effector poses come directly from the simulator state; ToyEnv provides a full top-down global map. A scripted grasp primitive attaches to the door handle when the end-effector is within 0.1 m. Training and evaluation use the same single layout.
extra: Best of 7 seeds (only 5/7 seeds solve the task); 11×11 grid; optimal shortest path averages 14 steps
ev: Sec. 5.3: 'Our best performing model achieves 100% success rate with average episode length of 19.2 steps.'
cmp_why: Custom environment; state given by design

t: Benchmarking Classic and Learned Navigation in Complex 3D Environments
eval_note: 340 episodes (10 fixed start-goal pairs per map) on MINOS split environments; episodes whose shortest path the simulator cannot compute are filtered out
method: Classic RGB-D (modular pipeline: ORB-SLAM2 + mapper + D* Lite + controller)
obs: Egocentric RGB and/or depth (depth range 0.001-4.0 m; 256x256 for classic, 128x128 grayscale 4-frame stack for learned) plus the goal vector relative to the agent (polar: distance and direction) at every step. 'Blind' variants get only the goal vector.
act: Discrete: move forward / turn left / turn right (apply linear/angular force in MINOS; continuous state), plus a 'Done' action triggered by a goal-distance threshold. Time budget 50 s = 500 actions.
priv: Main setting: none beyond the PointGoal specification, i.e. the goal's relative distance and direction are provided at every time step (acts as a perfect goal-relative GPS). Oracle ablations additionally give the classic agent the MINOS GT pose, or GT pose plus the MINOS map.
extra: non-learned; mapper thresholds/controller params tuned on train split; 500-action budget
ev: Table 3 (SPL, 'Classic pipeline performs well when provided with RGB-D input'); Table 11 'Average success rate'; Table 12 'Average pace'; Table 5
cmp_why: Main setting with protocol-provided goal info

t: Neural Modular Control for Embodied Question Answering
backbone: GRU master + GRU sub-policies, frozen PACMAN CNN + VQA

t: Translating Navigation Instructions in Natural Language to a High-Level Plan for Behavioral Robot Navigation
eval_note: Test-Repeated: 1012 new routes in environments seen in training
method: Ours with Mask and Ordered Triplets
obs: Text instruction + topological behavioral graph (triplets) + known start node; no visual input

t: Talk the Walk: Navigating New York City through Grounded Dialogue

t: Gated Path Planning Networks
obs: 2D: fully observed top-down binary maze map plus goal map (m×m; 4×m×m goal for Differential Drive). 3D: first-person RGB images taken at every position and all 4 orientations of the maze, plus goal map.

obs: monocular RGB (84x84 crop of a 60° view from a Street View panorama) + landmark-based absolute goal code (644-d) + previous action and reward
act: 5 discrete actions on the panorama graph: rotate ±22.5°, rotate ±67.5°, move forward to the next connected panorama
priv: No map, GPS or pose for the agent at test time. The goal is given as an absolute code built from distances between the true goal lat/long and 644 fixed landmarks. Heading labels are used only as a training auxiliary.
extra: Trained 1B steps with 25% of goal locations masked. Evaluated frozen for 100M steps only on goals in held-out squares of 0.01° (~1 km).
ev: Table 1: CityNav agent generalization performance ... on a set of held-out goal locations — row COARSE
cmp_why: No pose at test; held-out goals

t: Omnidirectional CNN for Visual Place Recognition and Navigation
eval_note: 3 held-out Unity scenes (2 home, 1 office); map from ~634 nodes/room, queries ~830 nodes/room
size: GoogLeNet-sized (parameter count not stated in paper)
obs: omnidirectional (equirectangular 360°) RGB image
act: heuristic local moves on a 9×9 neighborhood grid (move to position with minimal feature distance) after rotating by the estimated relative yaw (18° bins)
priv: The map of place exemplar images is given. The local navigation heuristic evaluates features at all 9×9 neighboring grid locations in simulation (local search by visiting positions). Real-world GT positions come from SfM and are used only for evaluation.
extra: average recall over error tolerances up to 1 m; per-tolerance values only in Fig. 4
ev: Sec. V-D: 'Our method achieves best average recall rate across different error-tolerance (69.7%)'; 'the inference speed of one query image is 123.46 ms, 128.21 ms, 2439.02 ms in O-CNN, NetVLAD, and Disloc'
cmp_why: Given map exemplars; local search visits neighbors

t: MINOS: Multimodal Indoor Simulator for Navigation in Complex Environments
eval_note: Empty (furniture removed) Small SUNCG houses (two-room houses), 10 episodes per scene
obs: Egocentric 84×84 grayscale camera (90° FOV, height 1.09 m) + goal signal (GT Euclidean distance and normalized direction for PointGoal/ObjectGoal; one-hot room class for RoomGoal). Multimodal variants add noise-free GT depth (0–10 m, byte-quantized) and 4 binary contact-force sensors.
act: Discretized {move forward, turn left, turn right} applied as accelerations (20 m/s², 4π rad/s²) in a continuous-state physics sim, ≈20 cm steps and ≈23° turns; 500-step episode limit
priv: GT Euclidean distance and direction to the goal (point, or closest point of goal object) given every step, via a perfect indoor-GPS-like signal. Depth is ground truth and noise-free. The DFP RoomGoal measurement uses whether the current room category matches the goal.
extra: Existing method benchmarked by the authors in MINOS; grayscale 84×84 + GT goal distance/direction; 13.2M training steps
ev: Table 2: Average episode success rate for agents trained on PointGoal and RoomGoal tasks, tested on novel environments (PointGoal SUNCG Empty Small row)
cmp_why: GT goal signal is the MINOS protocol

t: IQA: Visual Question Answering in Interactive Environments
